prerequisites: Complete courses 1.1–1.14: every system those courses built is running, course 1.13's fleet inventory is filed, and SBD-WSUS01 serves all four update rings.
Provision SBD-MGMT01 (10.0.70.10, VLAN 70) as a Windows Server virtual machine with a separate data volume (D: in this sample) for the record.

Keep the records earlier courses produced within reach: the service-path register, course 1.14's ring table and WSUS computer list, course 1.9's snapshot catalog, each course's baseline sessions, and the exception record.
labNote: Course 1.13 handed over a snapshot of the fleet; this course makes the whole network's component inventory a living record on SBD-MGMT01 — NIST SP 800-53 CM-8 in practice. The server keeps the record and reaches into nothing: the directory, the DHCP leases, the WSUS computer list, SBD-REPO01's records and the baseline sessions it is checked against arrive through the administrators' existing sessions. Endpoint agents and credentialed scanning, which would discover components on their own, arrive with courses 1.16 and 1.17. Column names and the monthly cadence are sample values; the system owner decides.

lessons.title: Design the inventory and its keeper
lessons.summary: Decide what the component inventory must hold before SBD-MGMT01 exists: every component inside the boundary counted once, and the columns that make each one accountable. Then name the records that can contradict it, and give it a keeper that holds the record without reaching into anything else.
objectives: Draw the inventory's boundary and list every component in it.
Choose the columns that make each component accountable.
Name the discovery sources and place SBD-MGMT01 under the tier model.
steps: Draw the boundary as CM-8 asks: every component of this network, each counted once, and nothing from outside it. That is every server and controller (SBD-ROOTCA01 included, offline in the vault), the three administration seats, each of the 50 PCs, the core and the VLAN 80 access switch, and the seven hypervisor hosts (SBD-HV01–SBD-HV07) on which Inside the Network places the virtual machines. The connected-side systems that fill the media stay out; the crossing records name them.

Choose the columns, one per attribute: name, type, role, operating system and version, domain membership, address and VLAN, OU, tier, location (host and rack), update source (a WSUS ring, an SBD-REPO01 snapshot, or by hand at a ceremony), latest baseline, the course that built it, an accountable owner by role (CM-8(4)), and status — planned, active or retired. Record the systems the design names but no course has built yet, SBD-EPO01, SBD-NESSUS01 and the four VLAN 40 servers, as planned, so a reconciliation never mistakes them for missing.

Name the records that can contradict it and what each one proves: the directory shows what joined the domain, the DHCP leases what is on VLAN 80 now, WSUS's computer list what reports for updates and in which ring, SBD-REPO01's catalog and access log which Linux servers take packages, and the baseline sessions which hosts have a measured state. Any disagreement is a finding, and lesson 5 makes the comparison a monthly check.

Place the keeper as Inside the Network does: SBD-MGMT01, Windows Server at 10.0.70.10 on VLAN 70 beside SBD-REPO01, a Tier 1 member server administered only from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 (rule A02). The model leaves its listeners to define: define them as management only, and give it no collection path of its own — source data arrives through the administrators' existing sessions, so the server that holds the record can't reach, or be used to reach, anything else. Its domain rows (F01–F03, F06 in Ring 3, F09, F17 and F18) already list it.
lessons.command:
# On SBD-ADMIN-SRV01: start the course record with the inventory's columns
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Evidence\management-server | Out-Null
'Name,Type,Role,OS,Domain,Address,VLAN,OU,Tier,Location,UpdateSource,Baseline,BuiltIn,Owner,Status' | Set-Content C:\Evidence\management-server\inventory-columns.csv
# SBD-MGMT01 isn't registered yet; its neighbour on VLAN 70 is
Resolve-DnsName SBD-MGMT01.sbd.test -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue   # expected: no answer
Resolve-DnsName SBD-REPO01.sbd.test | Select-Object Name, IPAddress   # 10.0.70.20
lessons.check: The boundary lists every component once, with the planned systems marked; the columns cover identity, place, tier, update source, baseline and an accountable owner; each discovery source is named with what it proves; and SBD-MGMT01's placement, administration and lack of any collection path are written down.
lessons.evidence: Keep the boundary list, the column definitions, the source table with what each source proves, and SBD-MGMT01's placement and administration decision.

model.label: SBD-MGMT01
model.text: The management tools server on VLAN 70 beside SBD-REPO01, with its listeners left to define.

quizzes.question: Why record the hypervisor hosts when every server is a virtual machine?
answers: They are optional decoration
They run every virtual machine, so whatever controls them controls the servers — they belong inside the boundary
The core requires it
quizzes.explanation: An inventory that lists the guests but not their hosts misses the components with the most reach. Inside the Network gives every server's host and rack for that reason.

quizzes.question: SBD-EPO01 is designed but not built. How does the inventory show it?
answers: It leaves it out until it exists
It lists it as active so the record looks complete
As planned, so the record matches the design and a reconciliation doesn't flag it as missing
quizzes.explanation: Status carries the difference between designed and installed. When course 1.16 builds it, the row turns active as part of that build.

quizzes.question: Why does SBD-MGMT01 get no collection path of its own?
answers: A server that can reach every source becomes a path to all of them; letting data arrive through existing administration sessions keeps it a keeper, not a hub
Collection paths are slower
Windows Server can't read other servers
quizzes.explanation: Least privilege applies to servers too. Every path the register doesn't need is one an attacker can't use.

recap: Every component inside the boundary, counted once — hosts and network devices included.
Columns that make each component accountable, owner included.
Sources that can contradict the record, and a keeper that reaches into nothing.
lessons.next: Lesson 2 builds SBD-MGMT01 and locks it down.

lessons.title: Build and harden SBD-MGMT01
lessons.summary: Build the inventory's keeper as a small, quiet member server, joined into the Servers OU so the hardening, tier and update policies apply from its first boot. It answers only the Tier 1 seat, and the record sits on its own volume behind permissions that admit administrators alone.
objectives: Build SBD-MGMT01 in its place with the network's policies applied from first boot.
Limit its administration to SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 and prove the limit.
Prepare the record's folders, permissions and version history.
steps: Build SBD-MGMT01 as a Windows Server virtual machine — on SBD-HV07 beside SBD-REPO01, where Inside the Network places it — with a separate data volume for the record (D: in this sample), the static address 10.0.70.10/24 with the core's VLAN 70 interface as gateway (10.0.70.1 in this sample), and both domain controllers for DNS. Join it straight into the Servers OU, so course 1.5's STIG policies, course 1.8's tier logon policies and course 1.14's Ring 3 update policy apply from its first boot.

Check that it took its place: time from a domain controller within course 1.3's threshold, and an update policy that names SBD-WSUS01 and Ring 3, with SBD-WSUS01 listing it there. Add it to SBD Event Sources from AdminJumpBox01, widen the collector's WinRM scope to 10.0.70.10 (F17) from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, and restart it so its security events reach SBD-SYSLOG01.

Close it to everything but its administration: Windows Defender Firewall on in every profile, and the existing Remote Desktop and Windows Remote Management rules scoped to SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 (10.0.60.20), because allow rules add up and a new, narrower rule would not restrict the broad ones. Install no other role and no agent; course 1.8's Servers OU policy already denies Tier 0 accounts here.

Prepare the record on D:: an Inventory folder with inheritance removed and full control for SYSTEM and Administrators only — the volume's inherited defaults let ordinary users read and create files — holding current, history, sources and findings folders. Every published version is copied into history with its SHA-256 in a hash list, and every change gets a line in a change log: who, what, why, and the change record it answers.

Prove the closure: a remote session from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 opens, the same attempt from SBD-ADMIN-PC01 fails at the core because rule A02 names only the Tier 1 seat, and the firewall's remote-address lists show only 10.0.60.20 for management.
lessons.command:
# In a session on SBD-MGMT01 from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
([adsisearcher]"(&(objectCategory=computer)(name=$env:COMPUTERNAME))").FindOne().Path   # ...OU=Servers,OU=SBD,DC=sbd,DC=test
w32tm /query /source   # a domain controller, never the local clock
Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate | Select-Object WUServer, TargetGroup   # Ring 3 - Member servers
Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup 'Remote Desktop', 'Windows Remote Management' -Enabled True | Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter | Select-Object InstanceID, RemoteAddress   # 10.0.60.20 only
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force D:\Inventory | Out-Null
icacls D:\Inventory /inheritance:r /grant:r 'SYSTEM:(OI)(CI)F' 'Administrators:(OI)(CI)F'
'current', 'history', 'sources', 'findings' | ForEach-Object { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "D:\Inventory\$_" | Out-Null }
icacls D:\Inventory
# From SBD-ADMIN-PC01: the same management path must fail
Test-NetConnection SBD-MGMT01.sbd.test -Port 5985   # expected: TcpTestSucceeded False
lessons.check: SBD-MGMT01 sits in the Servers OU with time from a domain controller, reports to Ring 3 on SBD-WSUS01, forwards its security events, accepts management only from 10.0.60.20 and refuses SBD-ADMIN-PC01, runs no extra role or agent, and holds an Inventory folder that only SYSTEM and Administrators can open.
lessons.evidence: Keep the OU placement, the time source, the update policy values and WSUS listing, the firewall scope, the refused connection from SBD-ADMIN-PC01, and the Inventory folder's permissions.

quizzes.question: Why scope the existing Remote Desktop and remote management rules instead of adding a narrow new rule?
answers: New rules are slower
Allow rules add up: a narrow new rule leaves the broad existing one letting everyone in
Windows allows only one rule per port
quizzes.explanation: Windows Defender Firewall admits a connection if any enabled allow rule matches. Narrow the rules that exist, then prove it from a seat that must be refused.

quizzes.question: SBD-ADMIN-PC01 shares VLAN 60 with SBD-ADMIN-SRV01. Why is its attempt on SBD-MGMT01 refused?
answers: Rule A02 names only SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 as the source for member-server management, so the core denies the Tier 2 seat — and the host firewall would too
Virtual machines can't use the network
SBD-MGMT01 is offline
quizzes.explanation: Sharing a VLAN grants nothing. The register names the seat, the core enforces it between VLANs, and the host firewall enforces it again.

quizzes.question: Why remove inheritance on the Inventory folder?
answers: To make backups faster
Inheritance can't be used on data volumes
A new volume's inherited permissions let ordinary users read and create files; the record should open to administrators alone
quizzes.explanation: Defaults are someone else's decision. The record's permissions are part of its integrity, alongside its version history and hashes.

recap: In the Servers OU: hardened, tiered and patched from first boot.
Management from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 only — proven by a refused attempt.
A record folder for administrators alone, with history and hashes.
lessons.next: Lesson 3 fills it with the first complete inventory.

lessons.title: Build the living inventory
lessons.summary: Course 1.13's fleet inventory was a snapshot of fifty PCs; SBD-MGMT01 makes the whole network's inventory a living record. Every component gets its place, ring, update source, baseline and owner, kept current by the procedures that change it.
objectives: Load every component into the inventory from the records the path already keeps.
Define how the inventory stays current and who owns it.
Publish the first version with its hash.
steps: Start from the records the path already keeps rather than from memory: course 1.13's fleet inventory for the 50 PCs (names, image ancestry, certificate thumbprints, sample status), the service-path register and Inside the Network for names, addresses and locations, course 1.14's ring table for the update rings, course 1.9's snapshot catalog for SBD-REPO01, and each course's baseline set for the latest baseline date.

Load the inventory with every component the boundary lists — the fleet, the servers (SBD-REPO01 included, with its current snapshot as its update source), the admin plane, the core, the access switch and the hypervisor hosts — each with every column filled: the CM-8 component inventory, in one place. Add the planned systems as planned.

Define currency: every build, move and retirement updates the inventory as part of its own procedure (CM-8(1)), so each later course's build lesson adds its rows, and a monthly reconciliation compares the inventory against the directory, the DHCP leases and the WSUS computer list — drift between them is a finding.

Name the owner — a role, with a named deputy — who approves each change, and publish the first version: copy it into history with its hash and log the change. Course 2.2 shows how a record like this one joins the Body of Evidence for the configuration-management controls.
lessons.command:
# In a session on SBD-MGMT01 from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, once the record is filled in
$inv = Import-Csv D:\Inventory\current\inventory.csv
$inv | Group-Object Status | Select-Object Name, Count
$inv | Group-Object Name | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | Select-Object Name   # expected: nothing counted twice
$inv | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'active' -and (-not $_.Owner -or -not $_.UpdateSource -or -not $_.Location) } | Select-Object Name   # expected: nothing
$stamp = Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd
Copy-Item D:\Inventory\current\inventory.csv "D:\Inventory\history\inventory-$stamp.csv"
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "D:\Inventory\history\inventory-$stamp.csv" | Export-Csv D:\Inventory\history\hashes.csv -Append -NoTypeInformation
lessons.check: The inventory lists every component in the boundary exactly once with every column filled, planned systems are marked planned, the update-on-change rule and the monthly reconciliation are written with an owner and deputy, and the first version is in history with its hash.
lessons.evidence: Keep the populated inventory export, the status counts and completeness checks, the currency rule with its owner and cadence, and the first version's hash.

quizzes.question: What makes an inventory 'living' rather than a stale spreadsheet?
answers: Pretty formatting
Update-on-change plus a scheduled reconciliation against sources that cannot lie — the directory and the leases
Monthly printing
quizzes.explanation: Processes keep it current; reconciliation proves it stayed current. Both are written down, so both are checkable.

quizzes.question: A machine appears in DHCP leases but not the inventory. What is that?
answers: Normal churn to ignore
A reason to restart DHCP
A finding — either an undocumented system or a broken process, and both matter
quizzes.explanation: The reconciliation exists to surface exactly this. Unknown hardware on the network is the classic first question of any assessment.

quizzes.question: Which control family consumes this record most directly?
answers: Configuration management — CM-8's component inventory is literally this artifact
Physical security
Awareness training
quizzes.explanation: The authorization path's CM controls ask 'what do you have and how do you know' — this lesson is the answer being built.

recap: One record of everything, with place, ring, update source, baseline and owner.
Every change updates it; a monthly reconciliation keeps it honest.
Owned, versioned, and ready to join the Body of Evidence.
lessons.next: Lesson 4 gathers what the network already knows, to check the record against.

lessons.title: Feed it from what the network already knows
lessons.summary: The inventory says what should exist; the network's own records say what does. Export the directory's computer objects, the DHCP leases, the WSUS computer list, SBD-REPO01's records and the baseline sessions through the sessions administrators already use, and file them on SBD-MGMT01 with hashes, in one shape lesson 5 can compare.
objectives: Export each discovery source through an existing administration path.
Know what each source can and can't prove.
File the exports on SBD-MGMT01 with hashes, in one comparable shape.
steps: Read the directory over LDAP from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01: every computer object's name, operating system, distinguished name (which gives its OU) and lastLogonTimestamp. Use an LDAP search rather than the Active Directory module, whose Web Services port the controllers open only to AdminJumpBox01, and read lastLogonTimestamp as a sign of staleness, not of last use: it is updated only when the stored value is 9 to 14 days old.

Export the leases on SBD-DHCP01 in a session from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01: every lease in the VLAN 80 scope with its address, client ID (the MAC address), host name, state and expiry. A lease shows what is plugged in now, joined or not; course 1.7's DHCP audit log shows what came and went between exports.

Export SBD-WSUS01's computer list the same way: each computer's name, address, last contact, last status report and requested ring. WSUS's cleanup removes computers silent for 30 days (course 1.14), so a machine missing there has been quiet for a month or more.

Copy SBD-REPO01's records over SSH as course 1.9 does, and count its web server's access log by client address to see which Linux servers actually take packages. List the baseline sessions in the evidence folders you hold, by host and date; Tier 0 reports its hosts' dates through the change record, because its evidence stays on AdminJumpBox01. Agents and credentialed scans that discover components on their own arrive with courses 1.16 and 1.17.

File the set: hash every export into a dated list, copy both into D:\Inventory\sources on SBD-MGMT01 through a remoting session, and reduce every name to one key — the short host name, so a lease's SBD-PC07.sbd.test and the directory's SBD-PC07 meet. Take all the sources on the same day; sources taken weeks apart disagree about machines that simply moved.
lessons.command:
# On SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 (Tier 1): one dated folder for this month's sources
$d = "C:\Evidence\management-server\sources\$(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd)"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$d\repo01" | Out-Null
$s = [adsisearcher]'(objectCategory=computer)'; $s.PageSize = 500
$s.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $p = $_.Properties; [pscustomobject]@{ Name = "$($p.name)"; OS = "$($p.operatingsystem)"; DN = "$($p.distinguishedname)"; LastLogon = if ("$($p.lastlogontimestamp)") { [datetime]::FromFileTime([long]"$($p.lastlogontimestamp)") } } } | Export-Csv "$d\directory.csv" -NoTypeInformation
Invoke-Command SBD-DHCP01 { Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId 10.0.80.0 -AllLeases | Select-Object IPAddress, ClientId, HostName, AddressState, LeaseExpiryTime } | Export-Csv "$d\dhcp-leases.csv" -NoTypeInformation
Invoke-Command SBD-WSUS01 { Get-WsusComputer -All | Select-Object FullDomainName, IPAddress, LastSyncTime, LastReportedStatusTime, RequestedTargetGroupName } | Export-Csv "$d\wsus-computers.csv" -NoTypeInformation
scp -r <your-account>@SBD-REPO01.sbd.test:/srv/repo-records/* "$d\repo01\"
# On SBD-REPO01: who fetched packages (RHEL family; /var/log/apache2/access.log on Ubuntu)
sudo awk '{print $1}' /var/log/httpd/access_log | sort | uniq -c
# Back on SBD-ADMIN-SRV01: hash the set and file it on SBD-MGMT01
Get-ChildItem $d -Recurse -File | Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 | Export-Csv "$d-hashes.csv" -NoTypeInformation
$m = New-PSSession SBD-MGMT01; Copy-Item $d, "$d-hashes.csv" -Destination D:\Inventory\sources\ -ToSession $m -Recurse
lessons.check: Each source export exists for the same date with the columns lesson 5 needs, the hash list matches the files copied to SBD-MGMT01, every name reduces to one key, and a note says what each source can and can't prove.
lessons.evidence: Keep the dated source exports, their hash list, the REPO01 access-log summary, the baseline-session list, and the note on what each source proves.

quizzes.question: Why read the directory over LDAP instead of with Get-ADComputer from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01?
answers: LDAP is faster for large domains
The Active Directory module needs the controllers' Web Services port, which only AdminJumpBox01 may reach; LDAP is a path every member already has (F03)
Get-ADComputer can't read computer objects
quizzes.explanation: The register decides which tools work from which seat. Reading what every member may read keeps the inventory owner in Tier 1.

quizzes.question: A PC has no lease today. What does that prove?
answers: That it was stolen
That it was retired
Little on its own — it may simply be switched off; check the audit log and the other sources before calling it missing
quizzes.explanation: Each source proves something narrow. Absence from one is a question for the others, not a verdict.

quizzes.question: Why reduce every name to one key before comparing?
answers: So SBD-PC07.sbd.test in the leases and SBD-PC07 in the directory count as one machine, not two findings
To save disk space
Because WSUS requires capital letters
quizzes.explanation: Most false findings come from formatting, not drift. Normalize once, in one place, and the comparison means something.

recap: Five sources, gathered through paths administrators already use.
Each proves something narrow; together they test the record.
Same day, one name key, hashed and filed on SBD-MGMT01.
lessons.next: Lesson 5 reconciles the record with the sources and proves the checks work.

lessons.title: Reconcile the inventory and prove it
lessons.summary: Compare the record with what the network reports, classify every difference, and prove the comparison catches drift before trusting a clean result. Then take SBD-MGMT01's first SCAP baseline and hand a reconciled inventory — and the monthly habit — to the courses that follow.
objectives: Reconcile recorded and discovered components and classify every difference.
Prove the reconciliation catches drift with a deliberate test.
Baseline SBD-MGMT01 and hand off the reconciled record.
steps: On SBD-MGMT01, compare the inventory's active rows with each source by the name key: the domain-joined rows against the directory, the VLAN 80 rows against the leases, and the Windows rows against WSUS's computer list and its rings. In a source but not the record is an unrecorded component; recorded but absent where it should appear is a gap; present in both with a different value — a ring, an OU, an address — is drift.

Prove the comparison works before trusting a clean result: run it against a test copy of the inventory with one PC's row removed — the PC must appear as found in the directory but not in the record — and against another copy with one ring changed, which the ring comparison must report. Test copies are never published.

Classify every real difference and close it: correct the record through the change log, bring the component under management or remove it, or record the explanation — a PC switched off for a week has no lease and isn't missing. An unrecorded device is reported to the system owner the day it is found (CM-8(3)), and drift that keeps coming from one procedure is fixed in that procedure.

Take SBD-MGMT01's first SCAP baseline with course 1.4's SCC and benchmark versions, run locally in a Tier 1 session from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, classify its open items as course 1.4 taught, and enter the date in its own inventory row.

Hand off: publish the reconciled version with its hash, set the monthly reconciliation in the week after course 1.14's cycle closes so the WSUS list is fresh, and note what later courses add — course 1.18 adds the VLAN 40 servers as it builds them, courses 1.16 and 1.17 will add agent and scan results as sources when they arrive, and course 1.19 carries D:\Inventory into the recovery set.
lessons.command:
# On SBD-MGMT01 (session from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01): the newest sources against the active record
$src = (Get-ChildItem D:\Inventory\sources -Directory | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -Last 1).FullName
$short = { $args[0] -replace '\..*$' }
$active = Import-Csv D:\Inventory\current\inventory.csv | Where-Object Status -eq 'active'
$directory = (Import-Csv "$src\directory.csv").Name
$leases = Import-Csv "$src\dhcp-leases.csv" | Where-Object HostName | ForEach-Object { & $short $_.HostName }
$rings = Import-Csv "$src\wsus-computers.csv" | ForEach-Object { '{0}|{1}' -f (& $short $_.FullDomainName), $_.RequestedTargetGroupName }
Compare-Object ($active | Where-Object Domain -eq 'sbd.test').Name $directory   # <= recorded only, => directory only
Compare-Object ($active | Where-Object VLAN -eq '80').Name $leases
Compare-Object ($active | Where-Object UpdateSource -like 'Ring*' | ForEach-Object { '{0}|{1}' -f $_.Name, $_.UpdateSource }) $rings
# Prove it: with SBD-PC07's row left out of a test copy, SBD-PC07 must show as directory only
Compare-Object ($active | Where-Object { $_.Domain -eq 'sbd.test' -and $_.Name -ne 'SBD-PC07' }).Name $directory
lessons.check: Every difference between the record and the sources is listed and classified, the deliberate tests were caught, unrecorded components were reported to the system owner, SBD-MGMT01 has its first baseline, and the reconciled version is published with its hash and the next reconciliation date.
lessons.evidence: Keep the comparison output, the classified findings with their resolutions, the tests that proved detection, the SCC results with classified findings, the reconciled version's hash, and the handoff note.

quizzes.question: Why run the comparison against a deliberately broken copy first?
answers: A clean result proves nothing until you have seen the same check catch a known difference
To make the report longer
Because the real record might be deleted
quizzes.explanation: A check that can't fail isn't a check. One planted difference, caught, turns 'no findings' into evidence.

quizzes.question: The directory holds SBD-PC51, which no record mentions, and it has a lease. What happens?
answers: Delete it from the directory and move on
It is reported to the system owner the day it is found and investigated as an unrecorded component, and the procedure that let it in is fixed
Add it to the inventory so the counts match
quizzes.explanation: Unknown hardware is the classic first question of an assessment. Making the record agree without asking why would hide the very thing CM-8 exists to catch.

quizzes.question: Why schedule the reconciliation after course 1.14's monthly cycle closes?
answers: Because WSUS is offline the rest of the month
Because the directory changes only once a month
Because the WSUS computer list and rings are freshest then, so a difference is drift, not timing
quizzes.explanation: Sources taken at the right moment produce findings worth acting on. Timing is part of the method.

recap: Recorded against discovered: unrecorded, gap or drift — each classified.
A planted difference, caught, makes a clean result mean something.
Reconciled, baselined and handed on — every month from now on.
lessons.next: That completes course 1.15. Courses 1.16 and 1.17, endpoint protection and credentialed scanning, are coming soon; course 1.18 stands up the business services and adds their rows to this inventory.
